title: Islanded-site operator contract and staged image provisioning PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define an operator-level contract and acceptance criteria for 'islanded' private/VPC sites that have extended or permanent lack of egress to Redwood control plane. Provide a staged, operator-driven image provisioning mechanism and upgrade flow that supports constrained networks, physical media handoff, and deterministic verification without outbound connectivity.

Scope: This ticket covers the product requirements and acceptance criteria for:
- Operator behavior when the site cannot contact Redwood control plane (islanded).
- Staged image provisioning (chunked images, signed manifests, checksum reconciliation).
- Offline upgrade acceptance: canary semantics, roll forward/rollback, and operator-managed health checks.
- Limited telemetry and delayed attestations.
- Operator APIs and UX expectations for Solutions Engineers and on-prem operators.

Out of scope: packaging/OS-level installers, physical courier logistics, and per-customer SOPs for physical media. Those will be separate implementation/ops playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Operator implements a deterministic manifest format: image manifest + per-chunk SHA256 checksums + canonical signing key ID.

When in islanded mode (no outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane for 10 minutes), operator must switch to 'offline provisioning' mode and accept staged images from a local registry or mounted media.
Staged provisioning supports resumable transfers: partially-applied image uploads resume from last verified chunk without full retransfer.

Upgrade can be executed with a 'staged canary' option: apply to a single replica/pod first, run health probes, promote if healthy, otherwise auto-roll back to previous image within configurable timeout.
Operator exposes explicit preflight checks: disk free space, certificate validity, KMS access (if present), and minimum kernel/OS versions; preflight failures block upgrade with clear error codes.
Image and manifest signature verification occurs locally using customer-supplied root of trust; verification failure aborts upgrade and leaves system in current state.

Operator must provide an audit log (immutable append-only file) of image provenance events: received-manifest, chunk-verified, manifest-signed-by, upgrade-start, upgrade-success/failure, rollback, with timestamps.

For islanded sites, operator stores telemetry locally and exposes a 'deferred-push' bundle that can be exported to a USB or mirrored repository when connectivity is restored; telemetry does not contain plaintext customer data by default.
All acceptance tests must run end-to-end in a simulated islanded environment (network partition) with both a local registry and physical-media ingestion path.
Operator API surface is documented in Confluence and includes endpoints for: upload-manifest, upload-chunk, verify-manifest, apply-upgrade, rollback, export-telemetry, and operator-health.
test_plan: Create a test cluster and flip the control-plane egress to blackhole for 15 minutes to simulate islanded behavior.
Push a signed manifest and image chunks to a local registry; use an interrupted transfer to validate resumability.
Run the staged canary upgrade: verify health probes, promote or rollback automatically based on failure thresholds.
Intentionally corrupt a chunk to ensure checksum detection and abort behavior.
Validate manifest signature check by swapping the signing key ID and asserting the operator rejects the manifest.
Export the deferred-telemetry bundle and prove it can be imported on a networked machine to replay events without exposing sensitive payloads.
Measure upgrade median time and 95th percentile in islanded versus normal modes; ensure thresholds meet SLAs (to be defined by implementers).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Solutions Eng runs staged provisioning flow with one pilot customer; operator logs and UX feedback collected.
Phase 2 (early access): Provide the operator binary and documented workflow to 3-5 customers with islanded requirements; collect upgrade/rollback telemetry.
Phase 3 (general availability): Release documented operator behavior in console docs and mark feature 'supported' in Private onboarding checklist.
During all phases, require a runbook for physical-media validation and an incident contact list for operator-level failures.
rollback_criteria: If post-canary health checks fail more than configured threshold (default 3 failures within 5 minutes), operator must automatically rollback to the previous image.
If signature or checksum verification fails at any stage, the operator aborts and rolls back any partial changes.
If disk pressure or critical service dependency (KV cache mount, KMS access) becomes unhealthy during upgrade, abort and rollback.
If operator observed error rate increases by >200% for core inference endpoints in 10 minutes post-upgrade, auto-rollback and flag for postmortem.

notes: Operator should treat 'islanded' as a first-class mode (explicit state) and not as an ad-hoc network failure. Engineering needs to provide a deterministic state machine and stable API contract so Solutions Eng teams can build customer runbooks. Consider a small telemetry shim that only records anonymized event counts and failure codes that are safe for export via removable media.
design_implications: Console UX must allow uploading a signed manifest file and show per-chunk verification progress. Error states must be actionable with clear remediation steps (e.g., 're-sign manifest with customer root key' or 'free 2GB disk and retry').
operational_notes: Support will require an 'islanded diagnosis' tool that can read the audit log, show last verified chunk, and produce a bundle for support teams. Provide Solutions Eng with a downloadable verifier binary for customers who want to pre-validate images before handoff.
security_considerations: Image signature verification must not rely on external OCSP checks while islanded. Any CRL/OCSP validation should be optional with clear opt-in. Root keys and signer chains must be supplied by the customer or stored in customer KMS; Redwood will provide guidance but will not have private key custody for islanded flows.
